A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModelSMC research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture validation, SIR model-discovery experiments, and kidney and Hodgkin–Huxley evaluations, including quantitative and token-efficiency results.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on the retained tasks, together with new Hodgkin–Huxley ablations, particle classification and posterior analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces unconditional categorical resampling with ESS-triggered systematic resampling and replaces geometric-mean likelihood weights with likelihood products. Appendix D changes two-stage feedback generation to one combined LLM call and introduces posterior-sampling importance estimation of marginal likelihoods, used for kidney and Hodgkin–Huxley experiments. These revise the reported procedure, beyond adding implementation detail.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 20-model, ten-dimensional Gaussian-mixture setting, synthetic SIR task, four kidney dietary scenarios and ten Allen database voltage recordings. The new analyses reuse these settings; changed target selections, particle counts and model configurations do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains FunSearch+ and ModelSMC N=1 for SIR and Hodgkin–Huxley, with only N=1 for kidney. However, the N=1 comparator explicitly shares the revised ModelSMC implementation, including the change from two feedback calls to one in Appendix D. This is a limited procedural revision of a retained comparator.

E3.justification: The default LLM changes from GPT-5 mini to Claude Sonnet 4.6. Discovery budgets, ancestry depth and FunSearch+ generation budgets change. Gaussian-mixture validation changes from copying-only propagation with up to 50 particles and 30 iterations to random replacement with 100 particles and 20 iterations. Reported likelihood metrics become totals rather than observation averages, and token-efficiency analysis switches from the best five runs to all ten.

E4.justification: Sections 4.5–4.6 add classification and analysis of 1,445 Hodgkin–Huxley particles, including channel-family rank stability, and ablations covering weighting, simulation budget, prompts, feedback, population size and LLM choice. Appendix G.1 adds weight-matrix and ESS diagnostics explaining finite-model behavior. These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond v1's existing examples and token analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions already report ten-run medians with 90% bootstrap intervals in Table G-1. v2 extends uncertainty reporting with bootstrap bands for token-efficiency curves and replaces Figure 2's mean/min-max presentation with medians and bootstrap intervals, labeled 100% in its caption. New ablations specify five seeds per variant versus ten for the default.

E6.justification: Main numerical results and rankings are replaced. For example, v1 reports average Hodgkin–Huxley marginal negative log likelihoods of 25.18, 28.96 and 25.95 for ModelSMC, FunSearch+ and N=1; v2 reports total values of 256.00, 254.58 and 243.27. These are under revised settings, not matched-setting performance changes. Conditional-likelihood result blocks disappear, while new ablation and posterior results are added. Figure 2 now shows oscillation below approximately 80% rather than concentration near 100%.

T1.justification: The main consistency theorem and most of its proof remain, but Appendix C extends the resampling argument to adaptive resampling. v2 removes the geometric-mean formula from Appendix B, adds the posterior-sampling estimator in Eq. D-36, and derives the expected 81% target-model proportion in Appendix G.1. As printed, D-36 uses posterior/prior importance weights, opposite to the ratio required by its stated sampling distribution and marginalization target.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: probabilistic model discovery, ModelSMC with LLM proposals, competitive discovery of interpretable mechanisms, and connections to SMC theory. Added analyses support these retained contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking finite-model oscillations to random replacement and ESS, interprets channel-family rankings as reproducible posterior preferences, and interprets the ablations as robustness to design choices. Token-efficiency discussion changes from ModelSMC matching or sometimes exceeding baselines to acknowledging N=1's lower median curves while qualifying conclusions through overlapping intervals.

D1.justification: Where v1 refers readers elsewhere for full prompts, v2 supplies extensive Hodgkin–Huxley propagation and feedback transcripts, simulator code, input/output constraints and response schemas in Appendix H. It also adds a prompting diagram, prior-construction guidance, particle-classification procedures and ablation configurations. These substantially increase reproducibility information; the code-access location and hardware disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Kitagawa's systematic resampling work and Claude Sonnet 4.6, and more explicitly positions the baselines as evolutionary versus sequential discovery paradigms. The broader related-work framing remains. Publication updates to existing references, including Jha et al., do not constitute new cited research.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain recognizable, with localized rewriting and clarification. Appendix D reorders prompting before parameter estimation, an appendix contents page is added, and new analyses and prompt examples receive dedicated sections. This expands organization without extensively rewriting the retained paper.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Figures 5, D-1, F-2 and G-3, plus formatted prompt and code panels. Figure 2 is substantially redesigned. The token-efficiency display changes from v1's six-panel Figure G-1 to three panels with uncertainty bands in Figure G-4. Tables 1 and G-1 remove conditional-likelihood blocks and reorder columns; existing scientific figures are also redrawn.

improvement.justification: The new ablations, explicit prompts and token-efficiency reporting across all ten runs improve transparency and empirical scrutiny. However, v2 introduces Eq. D-36 with a reversed importance ratio relative to Eq. 5, and Appendices F.3–F.4 explicitly say this estimator is used for the real-data experiments. The PDFs cannot establish whether this is only a formula typo or affects the updated results. That material reliability uncertainty prevents a confident net quality judgment despite the substantial additions.
